title: Cloak and Dagger
paragraphs: A wartime espionage anthology dramatizing dangerous intelligence missions and resistance work, drawing its atmosphere and subject matter from accounts of Allied clandestine operations.

NBC sustaining wartime-espionage anthology dramatizing OSS missions, based on the 1946 book Cloak and Dagger: The Secret Story of the OSS by Corey Ford and Alistair MacBain. The frozen set contains all 22 documented broadcast programs; no historical program is missing.

GRH documents the program through Sunday 4 PM period (May 7, 1950 to August 27, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Friday 8 PM period (September 1, 1950 to October 6, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Final Sunday broadcasts (October 15, 1950 to October 22, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Sherman Marks (director on 20 recordings), Louis G. Cowan (producer on 18 recordings and director on 1 recording), Corey Ford (creator on 17 recordings, performer on 8 recordings, author on 1 recording, and host on 1 recording), Alfred Hollander (producer on 14 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and director on 1 recording), Alistair MacBain (creator on 17 recordings and performer on 8 recordings), Jon Gart (music director on 16 recordings and music on 1 recording), and [[person|raymond-edward-johnson|Raymond Edward Johnson]] (performer on 16 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Office of Strategic Services clandestine operations, espionage, sabotage and intelligence work, World War II occupied territories, postwar dramatization of wartime intelligence, resistance networks and partisan support, and cover identities, deception and counterintelligence.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Korean War bulletin preceding The Eyes of Buddha, OSS wartime clandestine operations, 1946 Cloak and Dagger source book, and NBC sustaining espionage series.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (25 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (21 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (23 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]] (20 shared credited people), and [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (20 shared credited people).
